lessons.title: Equivalent ratios
lessons.label: Equivalent ratios
lessons.objective: Explain why multiplying both parts by the same number preserves a ratio.
prerequisites: Count small quantities and read the mathematical symbols used here.

curriculum.title: GCSE Mathematics 1MA1 — Ratio, Proportion and Rates of Change

tutorNotes.observe: Pause after each change. Ask the student to explain the picture before continuing.
tutorNotes.misconception: Doubling only one part preserves a ratio.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: What would happen if we doubled A but left B unchanged?

steps.title: Start with {{a|words}} part{{a|s}} and {{b|words}} part{{b|s}}
steps.explanation: A has {{a|words}} counter{{a|s}} for every {{b|words}} in B.

steps.explanation: Add one matching copy to each group. Both groups double together.

steps.title: The relationship stays the same
steps.explanation: {{doubleA|Words}} to {{doubleB|words}} is equivalent to {{a|words}} to {{b|words}}. Each group is twice as large.

scene.description: The groups remain in the ratio {{a|words}} to {{b|words}}.
